name: Fluid catalytic cracking and resid FCC
principle: Hot, fine zeolite catalyst behaves like a fluid and meets vaporised gas oil in a riser reactor at 470 to 525 °C, cracking it into gasoline, LPG, light cycle oil and slurry. Coke deposited on the catalyst is burned off with air in a regenerator at 590 to 675 °C, which reheats the catalyst for the next pass. Residue versions use two-stage regenerators and catalyst coolers.
key_equipment: flue gas power recovery and scrubber

advantages: Flexible between gasoline, LPG and propylene
Can process residues (RFCC up to about 10 wt% Conradson carbon per UOP)
limitations: Regenerator flue gas is a large CO2 point source
Catalyst fines and SOx/NOx need control
